Subject: Fwd: FinPartner latency spike after v3.2 rollout — immediate action needed

Team — forwarding FinPartner's alert (attached 95th_latency_report.pdf). Summary: their 95th latency jumped from ~320ms to ~920ms after the automatic rollout of rwd-infer-v3.2 (manifest: deployment-manifest-v3.2.json) in us-west-2 at ~08:45 PDT. Error rates for small payloads also doubled. Customer is asking for rollback and SLA remediation.

Questions / asks:
- Can eng confirm whether this meets our rollback trigger criteria (95th > 2x SLO or > 800ms for >10 minutes)?
- If yes, what ETA to route FinPartner traffic back to v3.1 for us-west-2? Any functional incompatibility risk?
- Priyom/Monica: please confirm with the customer that we will attempt an immediate traffic rollback and whether they want us to open a formal SLA exception/credit request.

Attachment: 95th_latency_report.pdf (customer-provided).

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Subject: FinPartner - sudden latency increase after model update
To: Support <support@redwood.com>

Hi Redwood —

We started seeing a significant latency regression across our production traffic shortly after you rolled rwd-infer-v3.2 yesterday evening. Attached is a short report with percentiles. Our SLAs expect 95th < 400ms; we are failing that consistently. Please advise urgent mitigation and whether you can roll us back to the previous model.

— Helen
Head of Platform, FinPartner Inc
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Helen Ramos <helen.ramos@finpartner.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinPartner latency spike after v3.2 rollout — immediate action needed

Hannah / team —

We see the signal in traces and can reproduce elevated 95th p99 for the FinPartner tenant in us-west-2 for rwd-infer-v3.2. Quick notes:
- Current numbers for FinPartner (last 15m): 50th ~ 78ms, 95th ~ 880ms, p99 ~ 1.3s. Baseline (v3.1) 95th historically ~ 320ms.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) up from 0.3% to 1.8% for small payloads.
- Initial triage points to an attention-kernel scheduling regression when sequence length < 64 on this kernel/version.

Rollback feasibility: we can do a per-tenant route override to send FinPartner back to v3.1 immediately (no code deploy required). Expected timeline: 8–12 minutes to flip routing + 10–20 minutes to see steady-state latency (cache/KV warm). Risks: short-term surge in GPU cycles and transient queuing; memory KV state won't be transferred so the first few requests will be slightly slower.

I recommend:
1) Execute per-tenant traffic override to v3.1 now as an emergency mitigation.
2) Open a revert-hotfix PR to disable the problematic kernel selection in v3.2; follow up with canary re-roll once fixed.

If CS approves, I'll trigger the override and post status updates.

— Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Update — rollback to v3.1 for FinPartner in us-west-2 executed at 09:52 PDT. Timeline and notes:
- 09:52 PDT: route override applied (100% -> v3.1).
- 09:54 PDT: initial traffic shows 95th ~ 760ms (warming).
- 10:06 PDT: steady-state 95th ~ 330ms, p99 ~ 420ms.
- No new errors observed attributable to routing switch; overall error rate back to ~0.4%.

I've opened INF-8392 to track the kernel scheduling root cause and a follow-up canary re-roll once the fix is validated. I'll attach a short postmortem and suggested rollback trigger thresholds.

Priyom / Monica: can you confirm the customer has visibility into improved latency and whether they want formal SLA credit/exception? I will keep a live dashboard link in the ticket.

— Marcus
